_meta.purpose: Reconciles the 13 dataset target_failure_type values against the 23 alarm codes AlarmService raises, so diagnosis and prediction never disagree about what a fault is called. Frozen artifact (sprint_plan 3.md §5), authored by Dhanuja.
_meta.status: DRAFT — Dhanuja must verify every entry, especially those with "review": true. Do not freeze until reviewed.
_meta.coverageRule: Every one of the 23 alarm codes must appear exactly once, either in an entry's alarmCodes[] or in diagnosisOnlyAlarmCodes[]. Nethmini's coverage test asserts this.
_meta.predictableMeaning: true = the dataset labels a pre-failure window for this type, so a model can forecast it. false = no dependable telemetry precursor (fire/intruder) or the alarm has no corresponding dataset target (diagnosis only).

entries.note: GEN_CRITICAL_FUEL grouped here as the escalated state of the same fuel-depletion fault. VERIFY: do you want critical fuel treated as the same predicted type, or as its own diagnosis-only code?
Rename only: dataset GEN_OVERHEAT == code GEN_HIGH_TEMP.
Rename only: dataset GEN_VOLTAGE_INSTABILITY == code GEN_VOLTAGE_ABNORMAL.
One-character mismatch: dataset ...FAILURE vs code ...FAIL. Same fault.

No dedicated supply-loss code exists; supply loss manifests as MDP_PHASE_VOLTAGE (phases collapse out of the safe range). VERIFY: (a) is MDP_PHASE_VOLTAGE the right manifesting code, and (b) supply loss is an upstream-ATS cascade — should it be predictable:false (reactive) rather than forecast?

AMBIGUITY: both SDP_BREAKER_TRIP and SDP_SUPPLY_LOSS surface as the single code SDP_PHASE_VOLTAGE, so an SDP_PHASE_VOLTAGE alarm cannot be reversed to one dataset type from telemetry alone. The correlation engine disambiguates: SDP_SUPPLY_LOSS co-occurs with upstream MDP/ATS alarms; SDP_BREAKER_TRIP is isolated. Assigned primary = SDP_BREAKER_TRIP (local, actionable). VERIFY the primary choice.

Shares SDP_PHASE_VOLTAGE with SDP_BREAKER_TRIP (see above). Left with no owned alarm code to keep the 23-code coverage a clean 1:1; identified at runtime by correlation with upstream alarms, not by an SDP-local code. VERIFY this modelling choice, or introduce a dedicated SDP_SUPPLY_LOSS alarm code in AlarmService.

Input power loss forces the UPS onto battery, so UPS_ON_BATTERY is its manifesting code. VERIFY: UPS going on-battery is often a NORMAL response during a mains transfer, not a fault — the correlation engine should suppress this when it coincides with an ATS source change (see the ATS-transfer correlation rule).

SEMANTIC CHECK NEEDED: dataset UPS_BATTERY_DEGRADATION = capacity loss over time (runtime/voltage decline faster than expected). Code UPS_BATTERY_LOW/CRITICAL = current charge below a threshold. These are related but not identical faults. VERIFY the mapping, or split degradation (predictive) from low-charge (reactive).
Rename only: dataset UPS_OVERLOAD == code UPS_HIGH_LOAD (load > 80%).
Dataset has one FIRE_ALARM type; the system raises a per-equipment fire code. Not forecastable — catalogue states no telemetry precursor. Excluded from model training (sprint_plan 3.md §6 rule 5).
As FIRE_ALARM. Digital input, no precursor. Diagnosis only.
